audit.whatIsWrong: Rated EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 37.5% win rate, while the late block opens 'This is where you lose, and the win rate shows it.'
audit.why: The page cites its own losing record in prose and rates the matchup even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows are wrong in both layers. Graves is given levels 1 and 6 and Maokai is given levels 3 and 4-5. The packet chart reads Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Skill / Maokai / Maokai / Maokai.
audit.why: whys[0] and whys[1] both describe Maokai owning the opener under rows saying Graves wins level 1 and level 2 is even. whys[2] calls level 3 'your genuine swing window rather than a clear loss' under a row handing it to Maokai — the chart is inverted at exactly the levels the text discusses.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group, with Twisted Advance's untargetability and the passive's cooldown rule written into the phases so the spikes carry real mechanics.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important line in Maokai's kit is absent: his healing passive's cooldown is reduced each time he casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL.
audit.why: It inverts the page's advice. Graves poking with End of the Line and Smoke Screen is actively refreshing the heal that beats him. The correct pattern against Maokai is to damage him with basic attacks — which are not spells — and to spend abilities on positioning, not chip. Nothing anywhere on the page says this.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[6], spikes[1], wants.you[0] and the mid block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable while he dashes — the page treats it purely as a root.
audit.why: It means a Collateral Damage fired as he commits is simply wasted: the shell needs a first champion to hit, and for the duration of that dash he is not a legal target. On a 100-second ultimate, that is the difference between the kill window the page promises and a lost lane.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[4], spikes[2] and wants.foe[0].
sources: enemyKit W text and untargetable flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is called a blind in seven places, including 'W's blind genuinely shuts off one of his autos'. Graves' Q appears as 'Q-cone', 'Q powder-cone' and 'Q powder-trail cone'. And his E resist buff is twice called 'Bushwhack armor'.
audit.why: Smoke Screen reduces sight range and slows on impact; it makes nothing miss, so the mid block's promise is simply false. Graves' Q is End of the Line, a single explosive shell — the cone belongs to his R. Bushwhack is not a Graves ability at all; his dash is Quickdraw and the resist stacks are True Grit.
audit.corrected: All three corrected in the strings I own.

edits.before: Maokai owns the first two levels — his saplings ward the lane and chip you for free magic damage, and you have no E charges yet to weave into your point-blank shell spread without eating a Bramble Smash knockback. Don't walk into a sapling field to last-hit; eat a little CS loss instead. Your one real swing is Level 3: E in, drop W on him so its blind eats his next auto, and detonate a Q cone point-blank, then dash out before his passive regen erases the chunk. Respect his Twisted Advance — if that root-dash glues you to him, no Bushwhack armor stack saves you from being stuck in melee with a tank.
edits.after: Maokai owns the first two levels — his saplings ward the lane and chip you for free magic damage, and you have no E charges yet to weave into your point-blank shell spread without eating a Bramble Smash knockback. Don't walk into a sapling field to last-hit; eat a little CS loss instead. Your one real swing is Level 3: E in, drop W on him for the impact slow, unload point-blank, then dash out before his passive regen erases the chunk. Respect Twisted Advance — he is untargetable through the dash, and once the root lands no amount of True Grit peels you off a tank.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your best and only window, and it's a coin flip. Your E charges and the magazine reset let you trade in melee, and W's blind genuinely shuts off one of his autos while cutting his vision — but his passive regen and saplings heal back most of what your shells chip. At 6, Collateral Damage plus your Dirk/Eclipse spike is the one clean kill: bait the Twisted Advance root, side-step his Bramble Smash knockback, then burst before his ult-empowered saplings rain down. If you can't kill him in this window, you don't kill him at all — note the blind only stops his autos, not his root or knockback.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your best and only window, and it's a coin flip. Your E charges and the magazine reset let you trade in melee, and W's impact slow holds him there — but his passive regen heals back most of what your shells chip, and here is the trap nobody tells you: that heal's cooldown drops every time one of YOUR spells strikes him. Poking a Maokai with End of the Line is paying for his sustain. Hurt him with pellets. At 6, bait Twisted Advance out first — he is untargetable through the dash, so a Collateral Damage fired into it is simply gone.

edits.before: This is where you lose, and the win rate shows it. Maokai builds full tank and his passive regen plus sapling sustain simply outlast your two-round magazine — you can't burst a tree faster than it heals. His Twisted Advance root pins you in his face while Bramble Smash knocks you out of your own shell range, and a blind does nothing against his ability damage. Your True Grit does stack MR as well as armor, so you don't melt to his magic — but tankiness doesn't win you a DPS race you lose to sustain. Take every objective, gank, and side-lane skirmish before his two tank items land, because after that he just zones you out of point-blank, the only range where you do real damage.
edits.after: This is where you lose, and the win rate shows it. Maokai builds full tank and his passive regen plus sapling sustain simply outlast your two-round magazine — and every spell you land on him shortens the cooldown on that heal, so the poke pattern that works everywhere else funds him here. Twisted Advance roots you in his face while Bramble Smash knocks you back out of your own range. Your True Grit does stack MR as well as armor, so you don't melt to his magic — but tankiness doesn't win a DPS race you lose to sustain. Take every objective and skirmish before his two tank items land.

notes: packet.suspectNames flags 'Twisted Advance' twice as a probable wrong name — both false positives, that is Maokai's real W. The genuine name errors ran the other way: 'Bushwhack armor' appeared twice for Graves' True Grit (Bushwhack is not a Graves ability), and his Q was called a cone in three places. Highest-value finding on this page is the one nothing on it mentioned: Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced when Maokai is struck by an enemy spell, so Graves poking with Q and W actively accelerates the healing that beats him — the correct pattern is to do damage with basic attacks and spend abilities on position.
